subject.title: Feature request: Read pinned Telegram messages via bot API

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram pinned-message reads, and should the first version be an explicit on-demand gated action/command or automatic session context?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent behavior decides how persistent Telegram chat content is authorized, exposed to agents, and optionally injected into session context.

options.title: On-demand gated action first
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned `list-pins` or read-pinned command/action backed by `getChat.pinned_message`, behind an explicit action/config gate and with no automatic injection.

options.title: Fold into broader Telegram read work
options.body: Track pinned-message reads under the broader Telegram message-read design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12756 and settle retained-history semantics first.

options.title: Defer automatic context injection
options.body: Keep pinned-message reads out of runtime context until maintainers approve an opt-in session-start injection and storage policy.

recommendation.title: On-demand gated action first
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned `list-pins` or read-pinned command/action backed by `getChat.pinned_message`, behind an explicit action/config gate and with no automatic injection.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible routing signal from recent Telegram action-surface history and prior product/security review context.
